lines: People complain that museums are difficult places to visit, but few visitors spare a thought for the difficulty of the museums' own task: **maintaining** their collections. Every object that enters a collection must be preserved indefinitely, and some of the most difficult items to look after are among the most ordinary — objects made of **plastic**.
人们抱怨博物馆是难以参观的地方，却很少有人想到博物馆自身任务的艰巨：维护馆藏。凡进入收藏的物品都必须被无限期地保存下去，而其中最难照料的，恰恰是一些最普通的物件——塑料制品。

sentences.en: People complain that museums are difficult places to visit, but few visitors spare a thought for the difficulty of the museums' own task: **maintaining** their collections.
sentences.zh: 人们抱怨博物馆是难以参观的地方，却很少有人想到博物馆自身任务的艰巨：维护馆藏。

sentences.en: Every object that enters a collection must be preserved indefinitely, and some of the most difficult items to look after are among the most ordinary — objects made of **plastic**.
sentences.zh: 凡进入收藏的物品都必须被无限期地保存下去，而其中最难照料的，恰恰是一些最普通的物件——塑料制品。

lines: Early radios, **sculptures**, pieces of Disney animation cels, artificial hearts: these and many other treasures are slowly falling apart. What makes the problem acute is that plastic is often the **signature** material of the very era that museums most want to document — our own. The work of conservators such as Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who spent decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands, has shown how serious the situation is.
早期的收音机、雕塑、迪士尼动画赛璐璐片、人工心脏：这些以及许多其他珍品正在慢慢解体。使问题格外严峻的是，塑料往往正是博物馆最想记录的那个时代——我们这个时代——的标志性材料。聚合物化学家西娅·范奥斯滕在荷兰文化遗产局工作数十年，她这类文物保护专家的工作已经表明形势何等严重。

sentences.zh: 早期的收音机、雕塑、迪士尼动画赛璐璐片、人工心脏：这些以及许多其他珍品正在慢慢解体。

sentences.en: What makes the problem acute is that plastic is often the **signature** material of the very era that museums most want to document — our own.
sentences.zh: 使问题格外严峻的是，塑料往往正是博物馆最想记录的那个时代——我们这个时代——的标志性材料。

lines: Van Oosten explains that the pioneers of plastics did not know how to mix their ingredients **properly**: some early products were, in effect, time bombs waiting to go off. An artist's foam **cushion** chair, for example, sheds tiny particles of polyurethane whenever it is used, while another object made of the same material **cracked** and disintegrated after being displayed under bright lights. The museum took it off display and put it in a dark storeroom to prevent further damage.
范奥斯滕解释说，塑料工业的先驱者并不懂得如何恰当地调配原料：一些早期产品实际上就是随时会引爆的定时炸弹。例如，一件泡沫坐垫椅每次使用都会掉落微小的聚氨酯颗粒，而另一件用同样材料制成的物品在强光下展出后便开裂、碎解。博物馆将其撤下展线，存入黑暗的库房，以防进一步损坏。

sentences.en: Van Oosten explains that the pioneers of plastics did not know how to mix their ingredients **properly**: some early products were, in effect, time bombs waiting to go off.
sentences.zh: 范奥斯滕解释说，塑料工业的先驱者并不懂得如何恰当地调配原料：一些早期产品实际上就是随时会引爆的定时炸弹。

sentences.en: An artist's foam **cushion** chair, for example, sheds tiny particles of polyurethane whenever it is used, while another object made of the same material **cracked** and disintegrated after being displayed under bright lights.
sentences.zh: 例如，一件泡沫坐垫椅每次使用都会掉落微小的聚氨酯颗粒，而另一件用同样材料制成的物品在强光下展出后便开裂、碎解。

sentences.en: The museum took it off display and put it in a dark storeroom to prevent further damage.
sentences.zh: 博物馆将其撤下展线，存入黑暗的库房，以防进一步损坏。

lines: Van Oosten and her team have developed ways of **stabilising** decaying plastic: they can apply a chemical 'sunscreen' to slow the damage caused by light. But the prospects for conservation remain **difficult**, and success is far from guaranteed. Meanwhile, we are living in the Age of Plastic, and the **decisions** that museums make today about what to keep and how to keep it will shape how people in the future understand the world we lived in.
范奥斯滕和她的团队已经开发出使正在劣化的塑料趋于稳定的方法：他们可以涂上一层化学“防晒霜”，以减缓光照造成的损害。但保护工作的前景依然艰难，远非稳操胜券。与此同时，我们正生活在塑料时代，博物馆今天就保存什么、如何保存所作的决定，将塑造未来的人们对我们所生活的世界的理解。

lines: Millennials were told that if they studied hard and got a good **degree**, a fulfilling job would be theirs for life. Young people entering the job market today — often called Generation Z — are no longer so sure. Higher education has become so **widespread** that the value of a degree has been dramatically reduced: in Britain, more than a quarter of graduates are in jobs that do not require one.
千禧一代曾被教导：只要努力读书、拿到好学位，一份令人满意的工作就能终生相伴。而如今步入职场的年轻人——常被称为Z世代——已不再如此确信。高等教育普及到如此程度，以致学历的价值大幅缩水：在英国，超过四分之一的毕业生从事着并不需要学位的工作。

lines: This is not to say that young people should not go to university. For those whose chosen **careers** demand it — medicine, law, engineering — a degree remains essential. But the research suggests that for many school leavers, going straight into work can be just as **rewarding**. Employers increasingly value experience and practical skills, and some firms have dropped degree requirements altogether.
这并不是说年轻人不该上大学。对于所选职业必需学位的人——医学、法律、工程——学位依然不可或缺。但研究表明，对许多离校生而言，直接就业同样可能大有收获。雇主日益看重经验和实用技能，一些公司甚至已完全取消了学历要求。

lines: When the science world asked its readers how they felt about **collaborations** between artists and scientists, the responses were strikingly positive: 'enlightening', 'challenging', 'stimulating' and 'fun'. In a survey carried out by a leading science journal, around 40% of **respondents** said they had already worked with an artist, and almost all who had done so said they would do it again.

lines: A frequently cited example is a **symphony** concert in Sydney, where climate data were woven into a reworked version of Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. The performance was praised for making science **accessible** in a way that raw numbers never could: audiences could hear, rather than merely read, what a warming world means. Such projects, researchers say, can reach people whom conventional science communication fails to touch.
一个常被引用的例子是悉尼的一场交响音乐会：气候数据被编入改编版的维瓦尔第《四季》。这场演出因让科学变得可感可及而备受赞誉——观众能够“听见”而非仅仅“读到”变暖的世界意味着什么。研究人员说，这类项目能触及传统科学传播无法打动的人群。

lines: Yet true collaboration is not as **simple** as scientists handing their findings to artists for decoration. For it to work, scientists and artists must design projects together, and each side must be prepared to **criticise** the other. Some artists complain that in practice they are treated as little more than illustrators of science, their own role undervalued.

lines: There are models worth following. The Center for Advanced Visual Studies at MIT brought artists and scientists together around a shared interest in **light** for decades, and produced work that neither group could have achieved alone. If such alliances are to be more than a passing fashion, researchers say, art-science collaboration must go beyond merely communicating science and aim at something **deeper**: the joint creation of new knowledge.

lines: New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 contains 'personal grievance' **provisions** that give employees a way to challenge their dismissal. The law says an employer must have a good reason to dismiss someone, and must follow a fair **process**. These provisions were designed to protect ordinary workers from being sacked without a legitimate cause.

lines: But the provisions have come to be applied far beyond that original purpose — right up to the **boardroom**. For highly paid managers, dismissal cases have become a way to test the reasonableness of any sacking, and employers complain that the process is slow, costly and **unpredictable**. Settling such claims is often cheaper than fighting them, so firms pay up even when the dismissal was justified.
但这些条款的应用早已超出初衷——一直延伸到高管层。对高薪管理者而言，解雇案件已成为检验任何一次解雇是否合理的手段，雇主们抱怨这一过程漫长、昂贵且难以预测。和解往往比抗辩更省钱，于是即便解雇本属有理，公司也宁愿掏钱私了。

lines: The Productivity Commission, a government **agency**, has pointed out the consequences: firms become reluctant to dismiss poorly performing managers, and poor performance at the top drags down the whole organisation. That hurts not just the businesses themselves but also ordinary staff, whose jobs and wages depend on the **health** of the firm. Ironically, the provisions may even make it harder for such managers to find new jobs, since employers fear the expense of dismissing them later.
政府机构生产力委员会指出了其后果：企业变得不愿解雇绩效不佳的管理者，而高层的低绩效会拖垮整个组织。受害的不只是企业本身，还有普通员工——他们的岗位和工资都系于企业的健康。颇具讽刺意味的是，这些条款甚至可能让这类管理者更难找到新工作，因为雇主担心日后解雇他们的代价。

lines: Other countries have dealt with the problem in a **practical** way. Australia excludes high-income earners from unfair-dismissal protection through an income **threshold**. sentences.en: Looking dismissive, the one on the left says: 'It is not in our major, so listening to it will be of little use.'
sentences.zh: 左边的学生一脸不屑地说：“又不是我们专业的，听了也没多大用。”

sentences.en: His companion, however, replies thoughtfully: 'Perhaps it will be useful after all.'
sentences.zh: 而他的同伴却若有所思地回答：“听了或许也有用。”

sample: The cartoon reveals a difference in attitude towards knowledge beyond one's own field. The student on the left represents those who confine learning to their own speciality and measure everything by immediate usefulness. The one on the right, by contrast, embodies the belief that knowledge is **interconnected** and that a lecture outside one's major may broaden one's horizons in unexpected ways. Many great breakthroughs, after all, have come precisely from crossing the **boundaries** between disciplines.
这幅图画揭示了人们对本专业之外知识的态度差异。左边的学生代表那些把学习局限于本专业、凡事以眼前有用与否来衡量的人。右边的学生则体现出另一种信念：知识是相互关联的，本专业之外的讲座或许会以意想不到的方式开阔眼界。毕竟，许多重大突破恰恰来自学科之间的跨界。

sample: In my view, the attitude of the second student deserves our applause. University education should cultivate versatile minds rather than narrow specialists. Attending lectures in other fields costs little time but may plant a seed of inspiration. If we remain **open-minded** to what seems 'useless' today, it may well prove valuable tomorrow.
在我看来，第二位学生的态度值得赞许。大学教育应当培养通识之才，而非眼界狭窄的专才。参加其他领域的讲座费时无几，却可能播下灵感的种子。如果我们对那些看似“无用”的东西保持开放心态，它们说不定在明天就会证明自己的价值。
